analysis.title: TotalEnergies SE (TTEF.PA) 3Q26: Strong refining and gas trading drive c.US$6 bn net debt reduction and a step-up to US$2.5 bn quarterly buybacks; remain Neutral on relative valuation
key_insights: TotalEnergies reported 3Q26 adjusted net income of US$9.1 bn on October 29, 2% above company-compiled consensus of US$8.9 bn. OCF (pre-OWC) was US$12.3 bn, 1% above consensus of US$12.1 bn.

The divisional beat came from Integrated Gas at US$1,885 mn post-tax (+5% vs consensus of US$1,800 mn, 2.3x qoq) and Marketing & Services at US$467 mn (+17% vs consensus of US$400 mn). Refining & Chemicals hit a record US$3,601 mn, in line with consensus of US$3,600 mn and nearly double qoq. Upstream operating profit of US$3,157 mn was 4% below consensus of US$3,300 mn.
The Board authorized US$2.5 bn of buybacks for 4Q26 and a further US$2.5 bn for 1Q27, up from the US$1.5 bn executed in 3Q26, consistent with the framework set at the September 2026 CMD.

The third 2026 interim DPS is €0.90, +5.9% yoy and in line with GSe. The company flagged a possible uplift to the final dividend of c.€0.20/share if FY26 cash flow lands at the upper end of the US$42-43 bn range. It reiterated its commitment to return 40% of cash flow to shareholders.
GS estimates dividend yields of 4.3%/4.6% and buyback yields of 3.3%/4.1% for 2026/27E. Total potential returns are 7.6%/8.7% vs the EU Big Oils average of 7.4%/8.4%.

Management guides the average LNG selling price above US$14/mmbtu in 4Q26 (vs US$12.3/mmbtu in 3Q26), reflecting the lag in oil-indexed pricing formulas. Management flagged a level closer to US$15/mmbtu given TTF around or above US$30/mmbtu.

Net debt fell by c.US$6 bn qoq, helped by a working capital release of c.US$3.1 bn. Company-defined gearing dropped to 9.1% from 13.1% in 2Q26. Net debt at end-3Q26 was US$21.9 bn including US$8.7 bn of leases.
GS-defined leverage (including hybrids and leases) is 16.5% (vs 22.3% in 2Q26 and GSe of 18.0%). GS expects it to be 16.5% at end-2026, above the sector average of 14.5%.
3Q26 FCF (pre-OWC) was US$7.5 bn vs GSe of US$8.2 bn. Organic capex of US$4.8 bn was higher than expected.

TotalEnergies has US$27 bn of guarantees on borrowings of equity and non-consolidated affiliates, the highest unconsolidated net debt among EU Big Oils in GS's analysis. Including these, 2026E ND/CE would rise to 32% vs the EU Big Oils average of 22%.

CMD 2026 net capex guidance is US$14-17 bn pa over 2027-2032, vs prior US$14-16 bn pa over 2027-2030, a c.US$0.5 bn/y increase at the mid-point. FY26 net capex guidance is maintained at c.US$15 bn, with US$11.2 bn spent in 9M26.

The company confirmed +4% pa total energy production growth through 2030 and >+3% pa Oil & Gas growth over 2025-2030. It set an ambition of +2-3% pa Oil & Gas growth over 2030-2035, with a plateau of c.3 mboed supported by a proven reserve life of >12 years.

For 4Q26, excluding the Middle East conflict, production is expected to grow by more than 3% vs 4Q25. The conflict impact is declining and is estimated at less than 5% of total production, mainly limited LNG exports via the Strait of Hormuz.
Refinery throughput is expected to be broadly comparable to 3Q26 (88% crude utilization vs 80% in 2Q26), helped by SATORP returning to normal, despite a 20-day turnaround at Normandy.

Integrated Power earned US$602 mn in 3Q26, in line with consensus, with CFFO up 7% qoq to nearly US$0.8 bn. The division is on track to be FCF positive in 2027 per the front page and by 2028 per the energy transition section.

GS estimates TotalEnergies' Low Carbon division is worth US$32 bn, or 14% of EV, which GS ranks second-highest among Big Oils on the front page and highest in the body text. About 30% of capex is Green under the EU taxonomy, rising to c.50% in 2030 on GS estimates.

TotalEnergies trades at 5.5x 2026E EV/DACF vs 5.1x for the group, a 20% premium, with an 11.8% FCF yield in 2026E vs 15.3% for the group. GS stays Neutral because it sees a better earnings trajectory and cash returns with attractive valuations elsewhere in the sector.

GS raised its 2026/27/28E adjusted EPS estimates by +6.4%/+6.9%/+3.7%, mainly on commodity prices. The 12-month price target rises to €90 (from €87) on an unchanged 7.0x EV/DACF multiple applied to 2027E cash flow, 6.4% upside from €84.60.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised to €90 from €87 on an unchanged 7.0x EV/DACF multiple applied to 2027E cash flow. Rating stays Neutral because the stock trades at a 20% premium to EU integrated oils on 2026E EV/DACF.

sector_views.rationale: TotalEnergies trades at a 20% EV/DACF premium to the group. GS sees a better earnings trajectory and cash returns with more attractive valuations elsewhere in the sector.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 adjusted net income reported at US$9.1 bn (US$9,064 mn) vs company-compiled consensus of US$8.9 bn (+2%) and GSe of US$8,453 mn. Adjusted EPS reported at US$4.07 vs GSe of US$3.79.

3Q26 operating cash flow (pre-OWC) reported at US$12.3 bn vs company-compiled consensus of US$12.1 bn (+1%), up 25% qoq. Reported 3Q26 net income was US$8,263 mn, after US$801 mn of extraordinary items.

3Q26 segment results reported post-tax vs company-compiled consensus: Refining & Chemicals US$3,601 mn vs US$3,600 mn, Integrated Gas US$1,885 mn vs US$1,800 mn, Marketing & Services US$467 mn vs US$400 mn, Integrated Power US$602 mn vs US$600 mn, E&P US$3,157 mn vs US$3,300 mn.
3Q26 FCF (pre-OWC) reported at US$7.5 bn vs GSe of US$8.2 bn. Organic capex was US$4.8 bn (reported), above GSe of US$3.8 bn.
3Q26 production reported at 2,474 kboepd (-1% yoy, +3% qoq) vs GSe of 2,475 kboepd. Oil production was 1,510 kboepd and gas production was 964 kboepd.

GS forecast: 4Q26E EPS of US$3.94 and FY26E EPS of US$13.15 (old US$12.35), FY27E EPS of US$11.89 (old US$11.13) and FY28E EPS of US$10.13 (old US$9.77). FY26E EBIT is US$44,074 mn (old US$41,410 mn).

The 4Q26 guide is an average LNG selling price above US$14/mmbtu, similar strong Integrated Gas performance, broadly flat refinery throughput and production growth above 3% yoy excluding the Middle East conflict.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Realized price for the quarter. Oil-indexed formulas lag spot, so the 4Q26 price should rise.

macro_indicators.reading: above US$14/mmbtu, with management flagging closer to US$15/mmbtu
macro_indicators.interpretation: Management guidance reflecting the lag of oil-indexed pricing formulas, with TTF around or above US$30/mmbtu.
Management cited current TTF levels as the reason the 4Q26 LNG price could be closer to US$15/mmbtu.

risk_factors: Lower or higher realisation in oil and gas prices vs GS estimates.
Weaker or stronger refining margins than GS expects.
Lower or higher recovery rates in mature offshore Oil & Gas fields, which would change decline rates, production growth and cash flow generation.
Execution difficulties or acceleration on key assets.
Leverage remains above the sector average (GS def. 16.5% vs 14.5%), and US$27 bn of guarantees on affiliates' borrowings are not in reported net debt.
Limited capex flexibility given the higher long-term capex guidance of US$14-17 bn pa.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 compares 3Q26 results to GSe and company-compiled consensus, with adjusted net income at US$9,064 mn vs consensus of US$8,900 mn and net debt to equity at 16.5% vs 22.3% in 2Q26.
Exhibit 20 shows 2026E metrics for TotalEnergies vs the 20-year average and EU Big Oils: EV/DACF 5.9x vs 6.5x average and 5.1x for the group, P/E 8.0x vs 10.3x average and 8.3x for the group.
geopolitical: The conflict in the Middle East is still reducing TotalEnergies' output. Its impact is now decreasing vs 3Q26 and is estimated at less than 5% of total production, mainly from limited LNG exports via the Strait of Hormuz.
The SATORP platform in Saudi Arabia returned to normal operations, supporting refinery utilization.

tension_points.bull_case: Superior 2026-27 and upstream growth with a >12-year reserve life, record refining and strong LNG trading, 4Q26 LNG pricing above US$14/mmbtu, and US$2.5 bn quarterly buybacks. Total potential returns of 7.6%/8.7% beat the EU Big Oils average of 7.4%/8.4%.
tension_points.bear_case: The stock trades at a 20% EV/DACF premium to EU integrated oils with an 11.8% FCF yield vs 15.3% for the group. Leverage is above the sector average, US$27 bn of affiliate guarantees sit outside net debt, and capex flexibility is limited.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Lower oil and gas price realisation or weaker refining margins than GS expects, since the price target rests on 7.0x EV/DACF applied to 2027E cash flow.

theme_stances.key_argument: Buybacks step up to US$2.5 bn per quarter and net debt fell sharply, but valuation carries a 20% premium and leverage stays above peers.
theme_stances.evidence: we remain Neutral rated on the stock

theme_stances.key_argument: Integrated Gas rebounded strongly in 3Q26 and the company expects similar performance in 4Q26 on lagged oil-indexed LNG pricing.
